ryan-cs: Heads up — Acme escalated a streaming failure. They see SSE stop mid-chunk (partial last data line), then client reconnects repeatedly which caused a billing spike. Happened from us-east-1 via Cloudflare + ALB. request_id=req_8f3a2.

anjali-eng: Thanks. Can you paste the exact curl and the truncated response? Any pattern on how long before the cut (seconds idle)? HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2?

ryan-cs: Repro curl they used:```curl --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=x"``` Output looks like: ```data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"text":"..."}}]}
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"text":"par"}}]}   <-- truncated mid-token then connection closed``` They report disconnect ~65-75s after last data was sent. Topology: Cloudflare (proxied) -> ALB -> origin. ALB idle was default 60s (customer said they bumped to 120 during test). Cloudflare proxying HTTP/2 to client and HTTP/1.1 to origin.

matt-eng: That timing smells like ALB idle timeout or CF buffering behavior. If ALB sends a FIN while client/CF expects keepalive, chunked SSE frames can be cut. Can you confirm request headers (Connection, Transfer-Encoding, Via, X-Request-Id)?

ryan-cs: Headers from Acme: `Connection: keep-alive`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Via: 1.1 cloudflare`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, `X-Request-Id: req_8f3a2`. They also had CF turned on with default HTTP/2.

sam-sre: Quick hypotheses: 1) ALB idle timeout closing TCP -> origin sees FIN -> runtime write returns EPIPE mid-chunk. 2) Cloudflare HTTP/2 multiplexing + buffering changes timing semantics so heartbeats from origin don't reach client as expected. Workarounds to try: set ALB idle timeout >= 180s for streaming endpoints; enable periodic SSE heartbeats (every 15-30s); or disable HTTP/2 at Cloudflare to keep behavior consistent. Also capture tcpdump on the origin to look for FIN from the ALB.

anjali-eng: Repro I ran locally: 1) start a streaming endpoint that emits a first chunk, then silence for 70s. 2) After 70s, attempt another chunk. Observed: when ALB (simulated) closed, server write returned a short write then `EPIPE` and our runtime logged a partial chunk header before the crash. I'll add logging around write return codes and chunk boundaries.

matt-eng: Please collect a pcap and the full origin-side logs for req_8f3a2. Command suggestion for customer / us: `sudo tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/sse-repro.pcap tcp port 443 and host <origin-ip>` and share the pcap alongside server logs. If ALB is indeed sending FIN, the short-term mitigation for hosted customers is to default ALB idle timeout=300s for stream routes. Long-term we should make our runtime more resilient to short EPIPEs and avoid emitting partial chunk delimiters when write fails.

ryan-cs: Will ask Acme to test with ALB idle=300 and to disable HTTP/2 at Cloudflare for a quick test. I'll request they produce a pcap and paste logs (they can send privately). ETA: EOD in their timezone.

deploy-bot: deploy: rolled out small logging change to streaming runtime to surface write errors and exact chunk sizes for SSE endpoints (PR #5123).
